target_customer: Organizations that would buy a modular quantum computer; not specified
problem: Quantum computers were built from separate components and not as a practical integrated system; AuroraQ aimed to assemble one from partner components.
business_model: hardware integrator selling integrated quantum computers sourced from partners (like Dell in PCs, per YC page)

competitors.name: Rigetti
competitors.what: full stack quantum hardware and software with the Forest platform

competitors.name: IonQ
competitors.funding_then: 22 million dollars per Network World list

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating quantum processing, communication and memory components into a practical machine was research-grade work needing hardware partners.

defensibility.rationale: An integrator relying on partner components has no obvious proprietary technology.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well resourced players were already building full quantum stacks; no action against AuroraQ specifically found.

market_need_then: Heavy public and corporate investment in quantum computing around 2019, but no evidence found of paying demand for an integrator.

branding.domain_note: auroraq.com did not respond (HTTP 445) at research time.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence found; name resembles many Aurora brands.

outcome_analysis: AuroraQ was a Winter 2019 YC company in Waterloo that aimed to build the first practical integrated quantum computer from partner components. YC lists it as inactive with a team of one. No post-mortem or closure report was found, so the cause is not public; an unsourced site speculating about a pivot is disregarded.
notes: Funding of 150K (March 2019; Y Combinator and Mehta Ventures per CB Insights) is from aggregators only and unverified, so no round is recorded. Location conflicts (Waterloo, Toronto, Kitchener). Competitor figures come from 2019 and later coverage; Rigetti and IonQ funding then is not stated. A possibly related Aurora Quantum Technologies at Velocity Incubator is unconfirmed. Website unreachable. Completeness pass: the $150K March 2019 round is recorded from Seedtable and CB Insights (two databases, same figure); Crunchbase shows about $149K. No press source found; this is the only round found.
